title: Surface record
description: One surface: identity, cross-references, its DEFINING DATUM, curvature condition, topology, symmetry, embedding quality, metrics and relations. Unlike a polyhedron, a surface has no exact vertex table -- its identity is the polynomial, parametrisation, Weierstrass data, nodal level function or variational problem that defines it. Meshes are renderings and are NOT stored; a reproducible recipe plus MEASURED invariants is stored instead. Records are families: most carry free parameters, and distinguished members live in `specimens`.

measure.description: A scalar with an exact closed form. `exact` uses a small fixed language: integers, + - * / and unary minus, parentheses, sqrt() acos() asin() atan() sin() cos() tan() cosh() sinh() tanh() exp() log(), and the constants pi and phi. It must evaluate to `value`; tools/surfdb_validate.py enforces that.

source.description: 'classical' (a published closed form), 'measured' (computed from a build at the stated resolution), or 'pslq' (recovered by integer-relation detection and verified by re-evaluation).

slugref.description: Slug of another record. May name a surface not yet in the database; the validator only checks reciprocity when the target exists.

varies.description: A field whose value differs across a parameterised family carries the literal string 'varies' at family level and its real value on every entry of `specimens`. The validator REQUIRES that a 'varies' field be resolved on every specimen, so 'varies' can never be used to avoid stating a value.

domain.description: Interval or set notation, e.g. '(0, inf)', '[0, 2*pi)', '{3, 4, 5, ...}'.

note.description: What this parameter changes -- and where it DEGENERATES. Boundary degeneracies are real and have cost time in this repo: the Hopf lift collapses at beta = 0 and pi, the Minding meridian quadrature converges only like h^(3/2) at the rim.

definition.description: How the surface is specified. Discriminated on `mode`. This is the record's centre of gravity, in the place a polyhedron record would carry `geometry.vertices_exact`.

mode.description: Facet F1. Determines which of the per-mode fields below are required.

fidelity.description: Whether this definition IS the surface or merely approximates it. Orthogonal to `exactness`. A nodal TPMS is an `approximation`: sin x cos y + sin y cos z + sin z cos x = 0 defines a surface that is NOT the gyroid -- it is a Fourier truncation whose mean curvature is wrong at the percent level. Recording this is what lets the validator hold exact definitions to 1e-8 while holding approximations to their own published residual.

approximates.description: REQUIRED when fidelity is 'approximation'. Index into the record's definition list: 0 is the primary `definition`, 1..n are `alternate_definitions`. Points at the definition that IS authoritative.

residual.description: REQUIRED when fidelity is 'approximation'. What the approximation actually costs, measured -- not asserted.

exactness.description: How the surface is EVALUATED, given exact data. 'elementary': closed form. 'numerical-integral': the Weierstrass zoo -- g and dh are exact, the surface is their integral. 'solved-parameter': a period condition pins a modulus as the root of a transcendental equation, so the value is a number plus a residual, not a radical. This is the analogue of polydb's `vertices_exact: null` for the snubs.

scale.description: The scale the stored expressions are written at.

polynomial.description: mode=implicit. F(x,y,z) whose real zero set is the surface, in the exact language. NULL where the equation exists but has deliberately not been transcribed -- a mistyped coefficient does not error, it silently produces a DIFFERENT surface with the wrong node count, so a null plus a `blocked_by` is strictly better than a guess.

clip.description: Many algebraic surfaces are unbounded; without a sensible clip they render as an uninformative slab.

domain.description: disk | rect | torus | half-plane | punctured-plane | punctured-torus | cyclic-cover

period_conditions.description: The residues/periods that must vanish for the surface to close up. The validator checks them: this is the sharpest test the Weierstrass block has.

associate_angle_degrees.description: Bonnet associate-family phase. 0 and 90 are the surface and its conjugate.

motion.description: A Darboux surface is the union of congruent copies of one curve. Translating gives a translation surface, revolving a surface of revolution, screwing a helicoid -- and a general rigid motion gives none of the three.

scale.description: The closed scale vocabulary, shared by `definition.scale` and `metrics.normalization`. Left as free text this reintroduces exactly the ambiguity polydb solved with edge_length_1 / midradius_1. 'published' = the source's own coefficients, unaltered (algebraic surfaces). 'unit_cell' = lattice constant 1 (TPMS, periodic). 'unit_waist' = neck radius 1 (catenoid, Delaunay). 'unit_radius' = generating or circumscribing radius 1 (quadrics, cyclides, torus). 'unit_scale_parameter' = the family's single scale parameter set to 1. 'unit_total_curvature' = scaled so the integral of K is -4*pi. NOTE: the repo's 'fit a 2x2x2 box' is a DISPLAY transform applied downstream and is never a storage normalization.

slug.description: Globally unique key across the whole database, regardless of which family folder the file sits in.

primary_family.description: The folder. Filing convention only -- the FACETS carry the classification. Rule: file by the property the literature names it for, ties broken toward the more specific folder. Contested classics are pre-assigned in the README so the build does not relitigate them (the catenoid is `minimal` not `revolution`; the hyperboloid is `quadric` not `ruled`).

families.description: GENERATED, not curated. Derived from the five facets plus primary_family and the topology block; tools/surfdb_validate.py regenerates and compares, so a hand-edited value is an error. Keys of index.json's `families` map.

ids.description: Cross-references into the sources surveyed, so a record is auditable rather than another undocumented dump. Null where the surface is not in that source.

mathcurve.description: Chapter stem in the local Ferreol mirror, e.g. 'ch1245_cyclidededupin_2'. Resolves offline.

weber_archive.description: Folder in the recovered indiana.edu/~minimal/archive/ tree.

alternate_definitions.description: The SAME surface by another construction -- never a separate record. Catalan's minimal surface IS the Bjorling surface of a cycloid; the catenoid IS the theta=0 associate of the helicoid; a Dupin cyclide IS an inverted torus. Index 0 is the primary `definition`, so entries here are indices 1..n.

condition.description: Facet F2, the STRONGEST condition by the declared precedence: minimal > cmc > cmc1-bryant > k-const-negative > k-const-positive > flat > willmore > constrained-willmore > weingarten > none. Necessary because the values are not disjoint: every minimal, CMC, flat and constant-K surface IS a Weingarten surface.

also_satisfies.description: GENERATED from the precedence chain. The catenoid is `minimal` and also_satisfies ['weingarten'].

total_curvature.description: The integral of K dA. For a complete minimal surface of finite total curvature this is -4*pi times the degree of the Gauss map -- an INTEGER multiple of 4*pi, which makes it a sharp validator target that catches a wrong Gauss map immediately.

measured.description: What the validator actually observed, PER DEFINITION. An approximation and an exact definition of the same surface produce different numbers, and reporting one figure for both is how a database becomes wrong.

genus_per_cell.description: For triply-periodic surfaces, the genus of the quotient by the lattice.

non_orientable_genus.description: The k of N_k, for non-orientable surfaces.

one_sided.description: MEASURED, not asserted -- the minimal-surface self-tests already gate on this.

ends.description: How many ends, and of WHAT TYPE. The minimal-surface literature indexes almost entirely by (periodicity, genus, ends), so the type matters as much as the count.

order.description: The k of an Enneper end of order k.

class.description: GENERATED: closed-orientable | closed-nonorientable | with-boundary | complete-finite-total-curvature | complete-infinite-total-curvature | compact-with-boundary | noncompact.

symmetry.description: Polyhedra have finite point groups and five notations cover them. Surfaces need five KINDS of group, because a triply-periodic minimal surface has a space group and a surface of revolution has a continuous one.

periodicity_rank.description: Facet F3. 0 = bounded/aperiodic, 1 = singly periodic, 2 = doubly, 3 = triply. Determines which notation applies.

schoenflies.description: kind=point. Field-for-field identical to polydb's block, so the two databases join on symmetry.

orbifold.description: Conway-Thurston signature of the AMBIENT group acting on R^3. Distinct from `intrinsic_orbifold`.

hermann_mauguin.description: kind=point (crystallographic) or kind=space (the space-group symbol, e.g. 'Ia-3d').

continuous.description: kind=continuous, in prose, e.g. 'SO(2) about z, plus reflection in z=0'.

point_residual.description: The discrete part of a continuous group, where naming it helps.

order.description: Order of the full group; null or 'infinite' for continuous and periodic kinds.

chiral.description: True when the group contains no reflections. A chiral surface is ONE record with a handedness parameter, not two enantiomorph records -- the opposite default from polydb, because a surface family is presented as one object with a handedness rather than as two catalogued solids.

intrinsic_orbifold.description: The orbifold of the SURFACE ITSELF as a 2-manifold quotiented by its own symmetries -- a different object from `orbifold`, and the thing EPINET's hyperbolic reticulation of the P/D/G surfaces is about.

generator_set.description: Which generator table tools/surfdb/invariants.py should substitute, when the Schoenflies symbol alone does not pin the group's ORIENTATION. C3v about the z axis and C3v about the body diagonal are the same abstract group and different coordinate substitutions; a polynomial symmetric in x, y, z has the second. Omit when the symbol is unambiguous.

verified_by.description: 'symbolic': the group generators were substituted into the polynomial or level function and it was unchanged -- exact, and cheaper and stronger than anything polydb can run. 'numeric': generators applied to a built mesh, Hausdorff residual measured. 'curated': taken from the literature, not recomputed.

quality.description: Facet F4. Matters more than it looks: bubbletons are not embedded (Kilian-Schmitt 2010), Tilted Scherk is non-embedded BY DESIGN (the Lopez-Ros tilt), and Boy's surface is an immersion of RP^2 that provably cannot be embedded. Typed, this turns 'it looks broken' into 'it is provably not embeddable'.

is_record.description: True when the surface is extremal for some counted quantity -- typically the maximum number of nodes for its degree.

fundamental_piece.description: Named, because a complete minimal surface has infinite area and a triply-periodic one has finite area only per cell.

aspect_ratio.description: Smallest bbox extent over largest. The repo's own collapse detector: a surface can pass every topological check and still have come out flat.

measures_note.description: REQUIRED where area or volume is null: says why. Infinite, or convention-dependent, or clip-dependent.

mesh_recipe.description: NOT a mesh. How to rebuild the surface, plus what was MEASURED from that build. Storing vertices would be storing one rendering at one resolution -- the same argument by which polydb omits nets.

specimens.description: Distinguished members of a parameterised family. Costa-Hoffman-Meeks is ONE record with a genus parameter, not four records. Every field the family marks 'varies' MUST be resolved here, on every entry.

slug.description: Set only where the specimen was PROMOTED to its own record -- when it has its own name, its own literature and its own symmetry group (Schwarz P, the gyroid and Schwarz D are three points of one Bonnet family and three separate records).

relations.description: The graph. Surfaces are far more related to one another than polyhedra are, and a large part of this database's value is the edges.

dual_labyrinth_graph.description: For a TPMS, the net threading one labyrinth, e.g. 'srs' for the gyroid.

polyhedral_analogue.description: A slugref into data/polyhedra/. The mucube is the polygonal ancestor of Schwarz P; saddle polyhedra span the same skew polygons as minimal surfaces; Schwarz's lantern is the standing caution that a polyhedral approximation's area need not converge.

same_surface_as.description: Suspected or confirmed identity with another record. Fischer-Koch C(S) and C(Y) were 'later recognised as the P surface and the D surface' (Brakke) and the repo ships them as separate rows -- so this field exists to record the claim WITH its confidence rather than forcing a silent merge or a silent duplicate.

check.description: The test that would decide it.

construction.description: AN ARRAY: one entry per shipping path, because a surface can be reachable from more than one operator. Verified cases: the Whitney umbrella ships parametrically in ruled_surface_generator and implicitly as the Hauser row in surfaces/algebraic; the helicoid ships in minsurf and in ruled_surface_generator; the catenoid ships in minsurf and as delaunay_generator's H -> 0 member. A singular block would drop all but one, and the validator's drive-and-compare would then regression-test only one route.

definition_index.description: Which of the record's definitions this path realises. The nodal and exact TPMS paths for the gyroid point at different indices and are gated at different tolerances.

blocked_by.description: REQUIRED where implemented is false AND the absence is a known obstruction rather than simply unbuilt work.

known_issue.description: Shipped, but with a caveat. The exact gyroid cell cannot currently be tiled watertight; Schwarz D exact tiling is ~6% non-manifold. A database that omitted these would claim more than the code delivers.

fabrication.description: GENERATED except for the overrides. developable follows from curvature.condition == flat; printable_watertight from embedding.quality == embedded plus compactness; requires_thickening from one_sided or a non-empty boundary. Only `self_supporting` is curated -- it is the one claim in the design that nothing can check.

definition.description: Where this record's formula came from. The critical provenance field: a mistyped coefficient does not error, it silently yields a DIFFERENT surface. Records must be DERIVED and cross-checked, not transcribed -- Mathcurve, the Virtual Math Museum and Hauser's gallery are oracles whose compilations carry their own terms, and this repository is published publicly. Cite them; do not copy them.

sources.description: Real mathematical attribution: the mathematician, the paper or book, the year.

verified.description: Claims recomputed by tools/surfdb_validate.py. Do NOT hand-set these to true.
